2. Facts, relevant for the purpose of the disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the present petitioner as pre-emptor filed the preemption case being No. 8 of 2007 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (in brief the SAT Act, 1950) in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Narail against opposite party No. 1 and proforma opposite party Nos. 2-5 for pre-emption of the case land. The case of petitioner, in brief, is that Fazel Mullah was owner of 55 decimals of land in plot No. 394 under BS Khatian No. 58 and SA Khatian No. 1707. There was homestead of him. The said land was recorded as homestead. Fazel Mullah died leaving 4(four) sons and 3 (three) daughters including the petitioner and wife Ranga Badu Bibi as legal heirs. After the death of his father the petitioner has been residing thereon amicably with other co-sharers. There are 6 homes in the land, garden and pond. Thereafter the brother of the petitioner Abdur Razzaque sold 15 decimals of land in the western side of plot No. 394 vide deed No. 2435 dated 10-10-2006 to Laki Mollah who is a stranger and there is rooms and kitchen of the petitioner. The petitioner being a co-sharer is entitled to get the land in question by way of pre-emption. 

 8. Mr. Bhattacharijee next submits that all the land outside of the municipal area would be treated as agricultural land as such there is no bar for pre-emption of the land in question under section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950. 

 11. On the other hand, Mr. Md Ahsan Ullah, learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptee-appellant submits that the learned appellate court below rightly held that preemption in respect of homestead is not maintainable under section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950. 

 12. He next submits that the cases referred by the learned advocate for the petitioner are not applicable in the instant case because all the transactions or execution of the deeds as referred in those cases were/have been done prior to the amendment by way of insertion of section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950. He further submits that the newly amended section 96 categorically ousted the provision for preemption of the homestead land. He also submits that it is admitted by the pre-emptor which is evident from the application of preemption itself as well as the SA Khatian No. 1707 and B.S. Khatian No. 58 that the land in question is homestead land and also both the court below concurrently found that the land in question is homestead land. Mr. Ahsan Ullah lastly submits that as per section 2(14) of the SAT Act, 1950 "any land connected with the homestead is also treated homestead land" therefore, the learned court of appeal rightly set aside the judgment and order of the trial court holding that the application for pre-emption is not maintainable as to the homestead. 

 14. On perusal of the judgment of both the courts below it appears that the leaned trial court allowed the application for pre-emption on the ground that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the land in question and the pre-emptee is stranger in the suit land. But the learned appellate court held that this application for pre-emption is not maintainable under section 96(16) of the SAT Act, 1950 as the land in question is homestead. 

 16. Now only point before me is to determine whether the piece of land which is homestead in nature situated in rural area can be pre-empted under section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950. 

 17. On perusal of the materials on records it appears that the land in question is admittedly homestead situated in the rural area. The pre-emptee purchased the land in question vide registered deed No. 2435 dated 10-10-2006. The amendment of the said section 96 of the SAT Act, 1950 came into force on 20-9-2016, therefore, it is very much apparent the amendment of the section 96 is applicable in respect of the present transaction and case. For better understanding section 96(16) of the SAT Act, 1950 is reproduced as below: 

 18. From the plain reading of section 96(16) it is crystal clear that provisions of pre-emption under section 96 is not applicable so far homestead land is concerned, therefore, it can be safely said that the pre-emption case so far homestead land under section 96 of SAT Act, 1950 is not maintainable. From the scheme of SAT Act, 1950 it appears that the section 96 is applicable for the agricultural land but 96(16) excludes the homestead land. 

 19. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the reasons as stated above my view is that the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narail has rightly held that the suit land being homestead, the application for pre-emption is not maintainable under section 96(16) of the SAT Act, 1950. Therefore, the learned Joint District Judge has not committed any error of law and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate court, does not call for any interference by this Court.
